notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I have no notes on Job 1 to give you. Every time I tried to open or search the sources, the tool told me no more calls were allowed in this turn. Because of that, I read none of the pages on your list (Enduring Word, Bible Hub's Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit commentaries, Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes, or the others).

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Writing notes now would mean doing exactly that, so I've left them all out rather than give you points I can't source.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll try to work through:
- **What each verse means (the traditional reading):** Enduring Word on Job 1, the Bible Hub pages for Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary, and Precept Austin's Job 1 page.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** each tradition's own sites, for example Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition (Reformed), Desiring God and Spurgeon (Baptist), Wesley's notes (Methodist), Sam Storms and Pneuma Review (charismatic), and 1517 (Lutheran). Likely topics are who "the sons of God" and "Satan" are (vv. 6–7), God's control over suffering (v. 12), and v. 21.
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship on "the satan" and the story's setting; Gregory the Great's commentary on Job (the *Moralia*) on New Advent and material on Catholic.com and OCA.org; and articles on Got Questions or Bible.org that discuss the word-of-faith teaching that Job's fear caused his losses.
